name: Raven desktop design tokens
design: Calm (chosen 2026-10-28): quiet, native, fine lines; micro-motion only, each caused by a real event. Reference: the Calm prototypes (concept-1-calm.html for the desktop apps, concept-1-calm-terminal.html for the terminal app).
note: Shared by the macOS (SwiftUI), Windows (WinUI 3) and Linux (GTK 4) apps; the terminal app reads the `terminal` section. Each app maps these names to its own resources. Light and dark values are given for every colour; apps follow the system appearance unless the user picks one in Settings > Appearance.

color.avatarRule: index = (sum of the bytes of the friend's Raven address) mod 5, so a friend keeps the same colour on every computer
color.pathRule: Path chips and route lines take their colour from the path kind: lan -> pathLan; nearby -> pathNearby; tor -> pathTor; internet, hole punched, 443 -> pathDirect; p2p, relay -> pathRelay; friend, handoff, letter -> pathFriend; anything else -> textSecondary. A chip is the colour on a 11% tint of itself (pill: 12% for icons on the Network page).
color.usage: sidebar: the friends column; surface: cards, incoming bubbles, the composer and the selected sidebar row; accentFillTop -> accentFill: the outgoing bubble (top to bottom); successFill: delivered checks, switches that are on, presence in touch; warningSoft: the away card and waiting banners; section*: the square icon behind each Settings section.

shadow.note: Offsets and blur in points; colours as #RRGGBBAA. Apps draw as many layers as their toolkit allows (at least the first).

label.note: names in the sidebar, Settings item titles

meta.note: times, tick text, the route line

sectionLabel.note: FRIENDS, GROUPS, the Settings group labels (tracking in em)

title.note: the chat header's name, sheet titles

brand.note: Raven next to the mark in the sidebar

pageTitle.note: Network, Settings and each Settings section (tracking in em)

display.note: the R A V E N wordmark (tracking in points)

mono.note: addresses, invite lines and the old security code

fonts.linux: system (Cantarell or the GTK default) / monospace

motion.rule: Honest motion: every animation is caused by a real event or state (status check, send attempt, signed receipt, incoming message, retry, presence change, node start) or by the user's own action (choosing a Settings section, a switch, a segmented control). The only decorative motion is the logo reveal on the welcome screen.
motion.reducedMotion: Follow the OS setting (macOS Reduce motion, Windows Animation effects off, GNOME enable-animations=false) and Raven's own setting (Settings > Appearance > Reduced motion); when on, no motion at all, only text changes: no springs, no packets, no spinners.

curves.note: cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2) as in CSS; y outside 0..1 overshoots (the spring). Toolkits without overshooting curves use the matching spring.

springs.note: The same motions as springs (response in seconds, damping fraction 0..1), for SwiftUI and the WinUI composition layer.

uses.bubbleLift: your bubble lifts out of the composer to its place (from the composer's position, scale 0.92, opacity 0.2), curve lift
uses.checkPop: the delivered check fills and pops (scale 0.4 to 1) when the signed receipt arrives, with one ripple ring (tickRipple); the path chip slides in from the left (chipSlide, curve chip)
uses.groupArc: a group message's ring: one arc per member, coloured as each member's copy is delivered (successFill), held (warningFill) or waiting (borderStrong)
uses.viewIn: a page or chat comes in: opacity 0 and 6 points lower to its place, curve arrive
uses.settingsGlide: the selection behind the Settings sections glides to the chosen one (curve glide); the old section leaves (sectionOut, 10 points, ease-in) and the new one slides in (sectionIn, 16 points, curve section) in the direction of travel
uses.segmentThumb: the thumb of a segmented control slides and resizes (curve thumb)
uses.switchKnob: a switch's knob springs across (curve knob) while its colour fades (switchColor); the knob stretches while pressed
uses.sheetIn: sheets rise 18 points and grow from 98% (curve sheet) over a blurred scrim (scrimFade)
uses.lockShackle: the lock icon's shackle closes before the locked window fades in (lockedFade); a wrong passphrase shakes the card (shake)
uses.radarPulse: two rings around the mark on the Network page, once per successful status check

motion.easing: ease-out for things arriving, ease-in for things leaving

terminal.note: The terminal app (node/crates/ash/src/tui): one palette for dark terminals and one for light ones, as 24-bit colours; terminals without truecolor get the nearest of the 256 colours, and No colors uses none (every state also has its glyph or word).
terminal.borders: rounded (╭ ╮ ╰ ╯ ─ │) in faint; the focused box in dim with a bold title

symbols.simple: for older fonts: braille becomes ·, ✓ becomes v, ♥ becomes +, ✉ becomes @, boxes stay
symbols.ascii: for terminals that draw box glyphs two cells wide: + - | for boxes, * o @ for marks, v for ✓, > < for packets
